meta.title: Your AI is Lying — RAG Fixes It

hook.text: Your AI just made up a fact. It sounded perfect. It was completely wrong.
hook.promise: Show how RAG grounds LLM responses in retrievable evidence to eliminate hallucinations

design.visualThesis: RAG eliminates LLM hallucinations by connecting the model to real documents through a vector-powered retrieval pipeline.
design.motionGrammar: Clean pipeline flows, document-to-vector transformations, similarity search arcs, and confident result reveals.
design.assetLanguage: Original SVG graphics, animated pipeline diagrams, vector space visualizations, and document retrieval flows.

scenes.purpose: Hook the viewer with the AI hallucination problem
scenes.narration: Your AI just made up a fact. It sounded perfect. It was completely wrong. In sixty seconds, I will show you the architecture that fixes this.

motion.action: A confident AI response with a verified badge shatters to reveal fabricated text underneath
motion.settle: Shattered badge fragments, red warning glow

scenes.purpose: Explain what hallucinations are and why LLMs produce them
scenes.narration: Here is the problem. Large language models generate text from patterns in training data. When they hit a gap, they do not say I do not know. They fill it with something that sounds right. This is called a hallucination.

motion.action: LLM brain icon generates text; gaps in knowledge light up with question marks morphing into fabricated confident text
motion.settle: Warning label 'HALLUCINATION' stamps onto the generated text

scenes.purpose: Introduce RAG as the solution that connects LLMs to real documents
scenes.narration: RAG fixes this. Retrieval-Augmented Generation connects your LLM to real documents. Instead of guessing, the model searches your actual data first, then generates an answer based only on what it found.

motion.action: LLM connects to a document database via animated retrieval arrows; documents flow into the prompt context window
motion.settle: Grounded response appears with a green verified badge

scenes.purpose: Walk through the complete RAG pipeline from ingestion to generation
scenes.narration: Here is how it works. First, your documents are split into chunks and converted into vector embeddings. These vectors are stored in a database. When a user asks a question, the query gets embedded too. A similarity search finds the most relevant chunks. Those chunks are injected into the prompt alongside the question. The LLM reads the evidence, then answers.

motion.action: End-to-end animated pipeline: documents split into chunks, chunks transform into vector dots, dots flow into vector DB, query arrow triggers similarity search arcs, matched chunks inject into prompt box, LLM generates grounded answer
motion.settle: Complete pipeline diagram with all stages connected

scenes.purpose: Show the result: grounded, citable, instantly updatable answers
scenes.narration: Now every answer is grounded. The model cites its sources. You can verify every claim. And when your data changes, the model knows immediately. No retraining required.

motion.action: Response panel with inline source citations that highlight back to original documents; a 'last updated: now' timestamp pulses green
motion.settle: Clean verified response with citation links and live update indicator

scenes.purpose: Deliver the one-line takeaway and engagement CTA
scenes.narration: That is RAG. Your LLM stops guessing and starts reading. What will you build with it?

motion.action: Clean architecture diagram of the complete RAG loop zooms to final state with audience prompt
motion.settle: Settled RAG architecture blueprint with CTA text

outro.takeaway: RAG grounds your LLM in real documents — it stops guessing and starts reading.
outro.cta: What will you build with it?
